## Your Turn

```{r}
fd <- read.csv("~/Desktop/School/Current Classes/INFO_3200/data/Accident.csv") |>
  clean_names() |>
  mutate(injury = ifelse(injury == 1, T, F),
         traffic_control = as.factor(traffic_control),
         weather = as.factor(weather))
```

1. Compute a summary table for these data

```{r}
#| label: summary-table

# Overall summary of the data frame
summary(fd)

# Counts of injury by traffic_control
fd |>
  count(traffic_control, injury) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = injury,
                     values_from = n,
                     values_fill = 0,
                     names_prefix = "injury_")

# Counts of injury by weather
fd |>
  count(weather, injury) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = injury,
                     values_from = n,
                     values_fill = 0,
                     names_prefix = "injury_")
```

2. Fit a naive Bayes model to predict the probability of `injury` conditioned on `traffic_control` and `weather`.

```{r}
#| label: fit-naive-bayes

nb_model <- naiveBayes(injury ~ traffic_control + weather, data = fd)
nb_model
```

3. Compute the confusion matrix.

```{r}
#| label: confusion-matrix

preds <- predict(nb_model, newdata = fd)

conf_mat <- table(Predicted = preds, Actual = fd$injury)
conf_mat
```

4. Compute the following summary statistics:
    a. Accuracy
    b. Precision
    c. Sensitivity
    d. Specificity

```{r}
accuracy <- .75
```

```{r}
#| label: classification-stats

# Treat TRUE (injury occurred) as the positive class
TP <- sum(preds == TRUE  & fd$injury == TRUE)
TN <- sum(preds == FALSE & fd$injury == FALSE)
FP <- sum(preds == TRUE  & fd$injury == FALSE)
FN <- sum(preds == FALSE & fd$injury == TRUE)

accuracy    <- (TP + TN) / (TP + TN + FP + FN)
precision   <- TP / (TP + FP)
sensitivity <- TP / (TP + FN)   # a.k.a. recall, true positive rate
specificity <- TN / (TN + FP)   # true negative rate

tibble::tibble(
  metric = c("Accuracy", "Precision", "Sensitivity", "Specificity"),
  value  = round(c(accuracy, precision, sensitivity, specificity), 3)
)
```

    The accuracy for this model is `r accuracy`.

*Reflection: the part that tripped me up was figuring out which class counts as "positive" — i kept second-guessing whether TRUE injury or FALSE was the one i should be predicting against. once i locked that in the precision/sensitivity/specificity formulas all kind of clicked. also kinda surprised how short the actual naiveBayes() call is, most of the work is in the confusion matrix math after.*
